Section Sequence: Hero with proof;What we do (2-4, unequal);Selected work;How it works;Who it is for;Contact
Hero Shape: Statement plus one credibility line. Left-aligned. Photograph or work sample beside it, not behind it
Rhythm: Tight through the middle, generous around work samples
Emphasis: Selected work — it is the argument
Notes: Trust comes from work shown, not adjectives. If there is no work to show, lead with the people

Section Sequence: Hero with what and where;Services;Area covered;Proof;Hours and contact;Map
Hero Shape: What you do and where, in one line. Phone number visible without scrolling
Rhythm: Even and calm — this reader is scanning for a phone number
Notes: A local visitor has one question and it is how to reach you. Do not bury it under storytelling

Section Sequence: Hero image with the offer;What is included;Dates or availability;Gallery;Reviews;Book
Hero Shape: Image-led, the place doing the selling. Overlay text only where the image supports it
Notes: People buy the place. Give photography room and keep the booking path always reachable

Section Sequence: Hero with the season or hero product;Categories;Featured products;Why buy here;Reviews;Newsletter
Hero Shape: One product or collection, priced, with a real photograph
Rhythm: Dense — a shopper wants to see stock
Notes: Nobody visits a shop for the brand story. Get to product within one screen

Section Sequence: Hero with the promise;The problem;How it works (3 steps);Proof;Objections;One action
Hero Shape: The promise and the action, nothing else competing
Emphasis: The single action, repeated three times at most
Notes: One page, one job. Every section either moves toward the action or gets deleted

Section Sequence: Plan comparison;What is included;Frequent questions;Contact for the rest
Hero Shape: No hero. Prices are what the visitor came for — start with them
Rhythm: Tight. A price page is a table, not a story
Emphasis: The plan you want them on — visually heavier, not just badged
Notes: Do not put a hero above prices. It delays the only thing on the page that matters

Section Sequence: Who we are in one paragraph;The people;How we work;What we believe;Contact
Hero Shape: A sentence, not a slogan. A real photograph of real people
Notes: About pages fail by being abstract. Names and faces beat values statements

Section Sequence: How to reach us;Form;Where we are;Hours
Hero Shape: No hero. The methods themselves are the content
Emphasis: The fastest contact method for this business
Notes: Show every method and let the visitor pick. A form alone loses people who want to phone

Section Sequence: Latest;By topic;Archive
Hero Shape: Optional. A one-line description of what is written about here
Emphasis: The most recent post, larger than the rest
Notes: Indexes are for scanning. Titles and dates carry the weight, excerpts help, images rarely do

Section Sequence: Title and context;Body;Related
Hero Shape: Title, date, author. Nothing else above the first paragraph
Rhythm: Reading rhythm — space between sections, not inside them
Notes: Measure 60-75ch, generous line height, real headings. Everything else is decoration

Section Sequence: What it is;Who it is for;What happens;What it costs;Next step
Hero Shape: The service named plainly, and who it is for
Rhythm: Even, with the step sequence tighter
Emphasis: What happens — the part people are unsure about
Notes: Buyers of services want to know the process. Vagueness reads as hiding the price

Section Sequence: The work first;The brief;What we did;The result;Next project
Hero Shape: The finished work, large, before any explanation
Notes: Show before telling. A case study that opens with a brief is a document nobody finishes

Section Sequence: What it does;The product itself;Key jobs;Pricing;Proof;Start
Hero Shape: A sentence a customer would say, plus the real interface
Notes: Show the actual product early. Abstract illustration delays understanding

Section Sequence: What you will learn;Curriculum;Who teaches it;Format and time;Price;Enrol
Hero Shape: The outcome, not the topic. What you can do afterwards
Rhythm: Structured — a curriculum is a list and should look like one
Notes: Learners buy outcomes and want to see the full contents before paying

Section Sequence: What, when, where;Speakers or agenda;Who it is for;Price and tickets;Location details
Hero Shape: Name, date, place, in that order, visible immediately
Rhythm: Compact toward the top, roomier for agenda
Notes: Time and place are the content. Anything above them is in the way

Section Sequence: Search;Sections;Recently updated
Hero Shape: No hero. Search and structure
Notes: Docs are navigated, not read. Sidebar structure and search beat any landing treatment

Section Sequence: What membership gives;Who is inside;How it works;Price;Join
Hero Shape: The membership benefit in the members' own terms
Notes: People join people. Show who is already there

Section Sequence: The cause;The need;What we do;Where money goes;Donate
Hero Shape: One human story or fact, and the donate action
Rhythm: Generous — this content needs room to land
Notes: Specificity persuades. One person's story outperforms an aggregate figure

Section Sequence: Where and when;Menu;Photographs;Book a table;Find us
Hero Shape: The place, photographed, with hours
Notes: People come for the menu and the address. Both must be reachable in one action

Section Sequence: Search and filters;Results;How listing works
Hero Shape: Search first. The hero is the query box
Notes: A directory that opens with marketing wastes the visit. They came to look something up
